newsitem.title: USA: Merisel files with SEC for restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Merisel files with SEC for restructuring.

text.p: Merisel Inc said Monday it had filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for a debt restructuring, including a one-for-five reverse stock split.

The restructuring would exchange $125 million principal amount of 12.5 percent senior notes for shares of "new" common stock representing 80 percent of outstanding equity, excluding warrants and shares subject to employee incentive options.
Existing holders of common stock would retain 20 percent of the outstanding equity. Each share of outstanding "old" common stock would be exchanged for one-fifth of a share of "new" common stock.
Holders of old common stock would also be entitled to receive warrants representing 5,263,736 shares, or 17.5 percent, of the new common shares to be outstanding.
After the restructuring, the warrants would be exercisable for shares on a one-for-one basis for a period of seven years from the completion date of the restructuring.
